_doc: The validation catalogue: every test, defined once. tests/common/control_center.py builds tests/out/control-center.html from it and from the campaign results; tests/common/catalogue.py --procedure writes procedure §6 from it. status: implemented | partial | planned | blocked (implementation state, not a verdict; verdicts come from campaign results). Amend here, then regenerate §6.

tabs.title: Test bench
tabs.question: Is the simulator setup trustworthy? The firmware block runs the real code at the right rate, measurements reach it, the PV panel equations agree.
notes: These establish the execution and measurement boundary using the same Core source. They do not validate the model or the firmware, and do not override a finding. [Implementation and prerequisites](../../tests/l1/README.md).

Contract **app-v1**, in `tests/l1/contract.json`, binds six physical probes plus VAC freshness and the three existing operator commands. Outputs include the stop/update action flags as well as duties/enables; relay and bridge request telemetry stays off. Unrun criteria are reported BLOCKED; measured failures stay FAIL.

tabs.title: Model
tabs.question: Does the model behave like the converter? Boost and inverter in open loop, firmware out of the loop; later compared with the same sequence on the board.
notes: Model tests run the power stages with the firmware out of the loop (duty or modulation imposed by the test). Their simulated verdicts check the model against hand calculations; the hardware comparison (same sequence on the board) is defined later.

tabs.title: Boost
tabs.question: Does the boost object do what it should, alone? L0 logic, then the object alone on the model.

tabs.title: Grid observer
tabs.question: Does the grid observer judge the grid correctly, alone? L0 logic, then the object alone through the model's grid sensing.

tabs.title: Inverter
tabs.question: Does the grid-following inverter library work, alone? L0 logic, then the library alone with a relay model.
notes: The L1 cases exercise library features the application does not use. They run the library through a small test-only harness, **not** through `controlStep`, so nobody reads them as application behaviour.

tabs.title: Application
tabs.question: Do the objects work together in the real firmware sequence? L0 control step, then the application on the full model.
notes: The [switched DCDC results](switched-dcdc-results.md) preserve the current regulation failure, numerical refinement and remaining coverage. Grid-injection cases are defined now and stay blocked while the application is synchronization-only.

tests.title: Build/runner failure before a reported criterion must fail the campaign
tests.criterion: Reported only when a build or runner fails before its criteria; its absence from a campaign of its level means that campaign ran.

tests.title: Inverter open loop, no load: filter behaviour
tests.criterion: INFO: .a output voltage vs modulation index, .b output spectrum peak 1–50 kHz (10 kHz lines of the 100 µs duty update excluded) vs the analytic resonance 1/(2π√(LC)) (L = AC inductors + choke differential inductance, C = C113 + damping capacitor)
tests.status_note: Implemented 2026-11-06: tests/l1/model_validation/test_model_open_loop.py (runs on demand, about 20 min on 8 cores)
tests.conditions: Ideal 400 V bus (boost disconnected); fixed 50 Hz sinusoidal modulation imposed on the bridge; relay open (filter unloaded)

tests.title: Inverter open loop into a resistor: modulation index sweep
tests.criterion: .a output fundamental within ±5 % of m·Vbus/√2 minus the first-order dead-time loss, a square wave of 2·td·f·Vbus in phase with the current (PASS/FAIL). INFO: .b output THD, .c output current, .d losses (bus power − load power, and the bridge share)
tests.status_note: Implemented 2026-11-06: tests/l1/model_validation/test_model_open_loop.py (runs on demand, about 20 min on 8 cores)
tests.conditions: Ideal 400 V bus; fixed 50 Hz modulation, index 0.2–1.0 every 0.2; relay closed on a resistor sized for 400 W at 230 V

tests.title: Inverter open loop into the grid: amplitude and phase steps
tests.criterion: .a P and Q within ±10 % of |S| of the 50 Hz phasor solution of the filter network, driven by the bridge voltage the simulation produced (fundamental of V(INV_A)−V(INV_B) over a full-resolution cycle) (PASS/FAIL, dead time 0). INFO: .b grid current THD, .c the same command with 100 ns dead time, .d the P and Q predicted from the ideal gate pattern instead, which shows how stiff the connection is: the bridge loses about 0.15 % of its voltage to second-order effects (C120 hard-switched at zero dead time), worth about 3 A at 0.17 Ω
tests.status_note: Implemented 2026-11-06: tests/l1/model_validation/test_model_open_loop.py (runs on demand, about 20 min on 8 cores)
tests.conditions: Ideal 400 V bus; modulation synchronized to the 230 V / 50 Hz grid by the test, duty updated every 100 µs as on the board; relay closed; commands aimed at P = ±200, +400 W and Q = ±200 var; 10 ns step (the filter impedance is about 0.17 Ω at 50 Hz, so 400 W needs only about 0.3 V between bridge and grid)

tests.title: Connection fidelity ladder: plant elements added one at a time (L, PLL, filter capacitors with contact on charged capacitors, 80 µs delay)
tests.criterion: .a which rung first produces the L1 connection trip; .b linear margins per rung; .c connection transient per rung, trip disabled. Reported for every case (INFO): peak line current over 10 and 20 ms after the contact; settling within ±0.05 A of the reference; |I_dq| seen by the controller against the line current; PLL deviation (largest angle and frequency excursion); for linear cases the loop diagram, open- and closed-loop Bode plots, crossover, phase and gain margins, closed-loop bandwidth and peak
tests.conditions: Averaged model (tests/l1/design/ladder.py, loop_linear.py): averaged bridge, 500 µH (r 0.1 Ω), library arithmetic (SOGI, park, PI, PLL, output advance), bench sequence from PWM_SETTLE, relay contact 9.7 ms after the command; candidate C (Kp 1 V/A, Ti 5 ms, current SOGI 2000 rad/s, advance 0.5) unless varied; IEC 60725 grid (0.4 Ω + 0.8 mH); current PI active from the relay command; trials: PI from the feedback, IAC low-pass 500 Hz, no advance, Kp 0.5
tests.status_note: Run 2026-11-10 on the IEC grid: loop linearly stable (PM 45°, GM 14–18 dB, bandwidth 160–170 Hz); the trip is the connection transient (1.3 A already on rung 1, 3.3 A with the PLL, 1.65 A with capacitors and 80 µs, 11.7 A at 100 µs)

tests.title: Source of the connection disturbance in the ideal case (rung 1)
tests.criterion: One factor at a time on rung 1: feedforward of the measured VAC vs the exact grid voltage; current PI on vs off; delay compensation 0 / 0.5 / 1 period. Identifies which path carries the 1.3 A transient. Reported for every case (INFO): peak line current over 10 and 20 ms after the contact; settling within ±0.05 A of the reference; |I_dq| seen by the controller against the line current; PLL deviation (largest angle and frequency excursion); for linear cases the loop diagram, open- and closed-loop Bode plots, crossover, phase and gain margins, closed-loop bandwidth and peak
tests.conditions: Averaged model (tests/l1/design/ladder.py, loop_linear.py): averaged bridge, 500 µH (r 0.1 Ω), library arithmetic (SOGI, park, PI, PLL, output advance), bench sequence from PWM_SETTLE, relay contact 9.7 ms after the command; candidate C (Kp 1 V/A, Ti 5 ms, current SOGI 2000 rad/s, advance 0.5) unless varied; rung 1 (ideal angle, no capacitors, delay one period); IEC grid
tests.status_note: Run 2026-11-10 on the IEC grid: the disturbance is the inverter-grid voltage mismatch at the contact, set by the output timing (1.5 periods of delay); exact feedforward with a 1.5-period advance removes it (0.016 A); today 1.29 A, best advance with the measured feedforward 0.7 (0.78 A)

tests.title: Contact angle: relay contact swept around the grid period
tests.criterion: Contact instant swept over 0–180° in 5° steps relative to the voltage zero crossing (the relay command shifted accordingly); best angle and flatness of the optimum against the relay closing-time spread. Hypothesis: the voltage across the contacts is the inverter-grid mismatch, proportional to dv/dt, so the voltage peak may beat the zero crossing. Reported for every case (INFO): peak line current over 10 and 20 ms after the contact; settling within ±0.05 A of the reference; |I_dq| seen by the controller against the line current; PLL deviation (largest angle and frequency excursion); for linear cases the loop diagram, open- and closed-loop Bode plots, crossover, phase and gain margins, closed-loop bandwidth and peak
tests.conditions: Averaged model (tests/l1/design/ladder.py, loop_linear.py): averaged bridge, 500 µH (r 0.1 Ω), library arithmetic (SOGI, park, PI, PLL, output advance), bench sequence from PWM_SETTLE, relay contact 9.7 ms after the command; candidate C (Kp 1 V/A, Ti 5 ms, current SOGI 2000 rad/s, advance 0.5) unless varied; rung 1, then rung 4; IEC grid
tests.status_note: Run 2026-11-10 on the IEC grid: the angle is second order with today's feedforward (1.17–1.70 A, no angle meets the target); with the synthesized feedforward the rung-4 peak falls to 0.09–0.38 A but a slow 0.4 A oscillation remains (PLL coupling); the PLL leads by one sample (1.8°)

tests.title: Blanking time after the contact: PLL and/or feedforward frozen
tests.criterion: During a blank time T_b after the contact (0–40 ms swept) freeze (a) the PLL (angle advancing at the averaged frequency), (b) the feedforward (Vd, Vq held at their pre-contact values), (c) both; time-domain judgement (time-varying), margins of the loop after the blank time. Reported for every case (INFO): peak line current over 10 and 20 ms after the contact; settling within ±0.05 A of the reference; |I_dq| seen by the controller against the line current; PLL deviation (largest angle and frequency excursion); for linear cases the loop diagram, open- and closed-loop Bode plots, crossover, phase and gain margins, closed-loop bandwidth and peak
tests.conditions: Averaged model (tests/l1/design/ladder.py, loop_linear.py): averaged bridge, 500 µH (r 0.1 Ω), library arithmetic (SOGI, park, PI, PLL, output advance), bench sequence from PWM_SETTLE, relay contact 9.7 ms after the command; candidate C (Kp 1 V/A, Ti 5 ms, current SOGI 2000 rad/s, advance 0.5) unless varied; best contact angle from D-GFL-03; rungs 1–4; IEC grid; swept: blank 0–80 ms, fade 0/10/30 ms, advance 0.5/0.3; contact 45° and 0°
tests.status_note: Run 2026-11-10 on the IEC grid (rung 4): advance 0.3 alone 1.44 → 0.66 A; best synthesized feedforward + PLL frozen 5 ms: 0.37 A peak; no case meets the target: an 80–90 ms tail from the PLL remains (Kp 2, Ti 20 ms: 0.32 A, 80 ms)

tests.title: Clamp after the park transform: feedforward and measured current limited around their pre-contact values
tests.criterion: Limit the per-period excursion of the feedforward (Vd, Vq) and of the measured current (I_d, I_q) from their pre-contact values, clamp level swept; time-domain judgement (nonlinear). Reported for every case (INFO): peak line current over 10 and 20 ms after the contact; settling within ±0.05 A of the reference; |I_dq| seen by the controller against the line current; PLL deviation (largest angle and frequency excursion); for linear cases the loop diagram, open- and closed-loop Bode plots, crossover, phase and gain margins, closed-loop bandwidth and peak
tests.conditions: Averaged model (tests/l1/design/ladder.py, loop_linear.py): averaged bridge, 500 µH (r 0.1 Ω), library arithmetic (SOGI, park, PI, PLL, output advance), bench sequence from PWM_SETTLE, relay contact 9.7 ms after the command; candidate C (Kp 1 V/A, Ti 5 ms, current SOGI 2000 rad/s, advance 0.5) unless varied; best contact angle from D-GFL-03; rungs 1–4; IEC grid

tests.title: Robustness of the best connection strategy
tests.criterion: The best combination of D-GFL-03…05 through rungs 2–4, the actuation delay swept 60–120 µs (80 µs is an assumption), on the IEC grid and through the cold and hot bulb (bench); selects the one or two candidates validated on the switched model (L1). Reported for every case (INFO): peak line current over 10 and 20 ms after the contact; settling within ±0.05 A of the reference; |I_dq| seen by the controller against the line current; PLL deviation (largest angle and frequency excursion); for linear cases the loop diagram, open- and closed-loop Bode plots, crossover, phase and gain margins, closed-loop bandwidth and peak
tests.conditions: Averaged model (tests/l1/design/ladder.py, loop_linear.py): averaged bridge, 500 µH (r 0.1 Ω), library arithmetic (SOGI, park, PI, PLL, output advance), bench sequence from PWM_SETTLE, relay contact 9.7 ms after the command; candidate C (Kp 1 V/A, Ti 5 ms, current SOGI 2000 rad/s, advance 0.5) unless varied; IEC grid, bulb 40 Ω and 500 Ω

tests.title: Voltage mismatch at the contact and the output capacitors
tests.criterion: .a mismatch across the open relay before the contact (amplitude, phase) in the switched runs and the averaged variants; .b fidelity: trip timing of the averaged variants against the switched model; .c resonances of the capacitor network and the switched model's spectrum after the contact; .d feedforward amplitude/phase error map; .e capacitor ablation (C122, C113, C7 branch, R3, a resistor in series with C113) with today's and the D-GFL-04 settings. INFO only
tests.conditions: Averaged model with the board's capacitor network (C120 1 nF, C113 120 nF, C7 680 nF + R3 4.7 Ω on the filter node; C122 120 nF on the grid side of the relay, reference/output_filter.png); rung 4, IEC grid, contact 45° (0° for the fidelity check); switched runs C-bench_iec and F-bench_iec reused
tests.status_note: Run 2026-11-10 on the IEC grid: the switched model's inverter side is +1.14 % / +0.33° above the grid before the contact (4.15 V; averaged −0.01 %); the closed-relay resonance (9.5–10.1 kHz) sits at the 10 kHz control rate and folds to 130–540 Hz; C7 + R3 is the essential damping; with C122 the averaged model disagrees with the switched one (trip 2.4 vs 6 ms), so capacitor results are indicative; switched runs proposed

tests.title: Invalid init or measurements never enable a leg
Leg 1 takes priority up to its current limit, leg 2 takes the excess, leg 2 is cleared when its demand stops
Cold-loop saturation sets the total current reference
MPPT perturb and observe: direction, turnaround at bounds, voltage ignored
STARTUP current clamp; STARTUP to BUSREG resets nothing; IDLE resets all
tests.criterion: .a STARTUP regulates toward VBusRef with the total current clamped to startupCurrentMax, leg 1 only; .b STARTUP → BUSREG keeps PID states, references and burst (leg 1 duty = an uninterrupted mirror PID); .c IDLE, and an active mode entered from IDLE, reset everything and start burst fully skipped

tests.title: Current-driven burst on leg 1
tests.criterion: .a from full skipping the skip count falls by one per hot loop while ILow1 < reference, then the PID runs; .b at minimum duty with ILow1 > reference skipping starts and follows the current error within [0, period]; .c the PID keeps its state across burst (duty held while skipping; continuous duty = an uninterrupted mirror PID); .d no burst while leg 2 has demand; .e a zero period is rejected and without burst leg 1 never skips

tests.title: Over-voltage full burst; over-voltage and over-current trip
tests.criterion: .a above 440 V every period is skipped and the PID held, below it the current error drives burst again; .b above 460 V the boost trips (legs off, outputs cleared), latched until IDLE; .c a leg current above 8 A trips, exactly 8 A does not; .d inconsistent settings are rejected, unconfigured protection never trips

tests.title: Voltage PID gain scheduled with VBusRef / VLow
tests.criterion: .a Kp = gain · clamp(VBusRef, 390, 410) / clamp(VLow, 24, 48) at each STARTUP/BUSREG cold loop, not in MPPT; .b scheduling does not reset the PID (total reference = an uninterrupted mirror PID with the scheduled Kp); .c inconsistent schedules are rejected

tests.title: Leg 2 starts only above a demand threshold; below it, off and leg 1's burst kept
tests.criterion: .a a leg-2 demand of one float step (4.8e-7 A) or 1 mA keeps leg 2 off, its duty 0, in BUSREG and MPPT; .b such a demand does not cancel leg 1's burst; .c a clear demand (1 A) still starts leg 2 with that reference; .d INFO leg-2 starts over a noisy 5.4–5.6 A ramp. Threshold value to choose (#5)
